Here is a factual research note on the event “Cold water supply restored to 29 apartment buildings in Ivanovo” as of November 23, 2026:

---

## What happened

- On **23 November 2026**, a **communal water supply failure** occurred at address **ulitsa Minskaya, 92 in Ivanovo**.([now37.ru](https://now37.ru/news/20261123/v-ivanove-iz-za-povrezhdeniya-vodosnabzheniya-bez-kholodnoy-vody-ostayutsya-29-domov-i-dva-detsada?utm_source=openai))  
- As a result, **cold water supply (ХВС — холодное водоснабжение)** was **temporarily disrupted** in:
  - **29 multi-apartment residential buildings**,
  - Two **socially significant institutions**: **kindergartens No. 37 and No. 191**,  
  - Affecting about **2,150 residents**.([i3vestno.ru](https://i3vestno.ru/news/2026/11/23/v_ivanove_29_mkd_ostalis_bez_vody_iz_za_povrezhdeniya_seti_hvs_na_minskoy_ulice?utm_source=openai))  

- The disruption was caused by damage to an **underground (subterranean) cold water main** (водовод подземного залегания) near this address.([i3vestno.ru](https://i3vestno.ru/news/2026/11/23/v_ivanove_29_mkd_ostalis_bez_vody_iz_za_povrezhdeniya_seti_hvs_na_minskoy_ulice?utm_source=openai))  

- **Repair works** were underway by crews, involving **13 people** and **5 pieces of specialized equipment**.([i3vestno.ru](https://i3vestno.ru/news/2026/11/23/v_ivanove_29_mkd_ostalis_bez_vody_iz_za_povrezhdeniya_seti_hvs_na_minskoy_ulice?utm_source=openai))  

- The **expected time** for completion of the emergency repair works was set for **23:59 (midnight) on 23 November 2026**.([i3vestno.ru](https://i3vestno.ru/news/2026/11/23/v_ivanove_29_mkd_ostalis_bez_vody_iz_za_povrezhdeniya_seti_hvs_na_minskoy_ulice?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Outcome / current status

- By **20:50 local time** on 23 November 2026, reports from MChS (the regional Ministry for Emergency Situations) stated that **cold water supply had been restored** to all affected 29 apartment buildings and the two kindergartens.([kstati.news](https://kstati.news/news/society/v-29-domakh-i-2-detsadakh-v-ivanove-vosstanovili-kholodnoe-vodosnabzhenie/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Sources and confirmation

- Independent regional news outlets such as *Kstati.news* and *NewsIvanovo* reported on both the outage and restoration using statements from **Государственное управление МЧС по Ивановской области** (the regional emergency services) as the primary source.([kstati.news](https://kstati.news/news/society/v-29-domakh-i-2-detsadakh-v-ivanove-vosstanovili-kholodnoe-vodosnabzhenie/?utm_source=openai))  
- The outlet *i3vestno.ru* also reported on the outage, including technical details about the cause and the expected restoration time.([i3vestno.ru](https://i3vestno.ru/news/2026/11/23/v_ivanove_29_mkd_ostalis_bez_vody_iz_za_povrezhdeniya_seti_hvs_na_minskoy_ulice?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Key figures and timeline

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Number of apartment buildings affected | 29 multi-apartment buildings |
| Social institutions affected | 2 kindergartens (No. 37 & No. 191) |
| Estimated number of people without water | ~2,150 residents |
| Cause | Damage to underground cold water main at ulitsa Minskaya, 92 |
| Repair resources deployed | 13 people, 5 specialized equipment units |
| Expected repair completion | By 23:59 on 23 Nov 2026 |
| Actual restoration reported | By ~20:50 on 23 Nov 2026 |

---

If you want, I can also try to locate any official municipal or governmental document confirming the restoration (e.g. a press release from MChS), or track whether there were any follow-ups (e.g. investigations, compensations).

Here’s a research note on what actually happened with the walrus conservation story. All facts below are drawn from primary sources or independent journalism; I’ve distinguished completed outcomes from plans or proposals, and noted where multiple outlets derive their stories from the same releases.

---

## What Happened  
- On **November 18, 2026**, *The Conservation Fund* announced it had secured a **permanent conservation easement** over **47,473 acres** (≈ 19,210 hectares) of land around **Point Lay**, northwest Alaska, including barrier islands used by Pacific walruses. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  
- The land rights are held by the **Cully Corporation**, an Alaska Native Village Corporation. Under the easement, the land remains owned by Cully Corporation, but certain development rights (e.g. coal and gravel extraction) are permanently restricted. The easement will be held and managed by the **Interior Alaska Land Trust**. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Figures and Context  
- The site supports **more than 200,000 Pacific walruses**, particularly females and young, which now gather annually on these islands—a haul-out made necessary by loss of sea ice. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  
- This is now the **largest Pacific walrus haul-out in North America**. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Why It Was Done  
- The conservation easement aims to reduce **human disturbances**—including from industrial development (coal/gravel), tourism, and aircraft—that can trigger stampedes among walruses. These stampedes have in past events resulted in **hundreds or thousands of juvenile deaths**. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  
- At the same time, subsistence use by local Indigenous communities (the Inupiaq at Point Lay) is preserved, including continued access to natural resources and cultural use. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## The Outcome vs. What Was Pledged or Planned  
- **Completed/measured outcome**: The conservation easement has been signed and established, covering 47,473 acres. The legal restrictions are in place. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Not** just a plan or pledge—this is now active protection under the easement.  
- **Payment amount** was **not disclosed** in any public source. ([alaskanews.com](https://alaskanews.com/c/alaska-news/point-lay-village-corporation-sells-permanent-easement-around-walrus-haulout?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent vs. Primary Sources  
- **Primary source**: The Conservation Fund’s press release, titled *“The Conservation Fund Permanently Protects Critical Pacific Walrus Habitat”* published Nov. 18, 2026. ([conservationfund.org](https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/press-room/the-conservation-fund-permanently-protects-critical-pacific-walrus-habitat/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Independent sources**:  
   • CNN article covering the announcement. ([accuweather.com](https://www.accuweather.com/en/climate/200000-walruses-are-forced-ashore-in-alaska-as-sea-ice-melts-now-theres-a-plan-to-protect-them/1960856?utm_source=openai))  
   • Alaska News reporting on the sale of the easement by Cully Corporation. ([alaskanews.com](https://alaskanews.com/c/alaska-news/point-lay-village-corporation-sells-permanent-easement-around-walrus-haulout?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you like, I can also check if there are scientific assessments or follow-up studies to see how effective the protection has been since the easement was put in place.

Here’s a research note on the candidate claim:

---

## Research Note: “46% decrease in domestic violence cases reported”

**Claim:** A 46% decrease globally in reported domestic violence cases.  
**Country:** “Global”  
**Date:** November 23, 2026  
**Category:** People

---

## Findings

### What was found

1. **No confirmation of a 46% global decrease**  
   - Searches did **not** turn up credible international or multilateral reports confirming a 46% drop in domestic violence cases globally.  
   - Global data from the UNAIDS brief indicates there has *not been significant progress* in reducing domestic violence prevalence worldwide since 2000. Prevalence figures: ~17.8% in 2000, ~17.5% in 2010, ~14.4% in 2018, ~13.7% in 2023. ([unaids.org](https://unaids.org/sites/default/files/2026-06/20260612_global_aids_brief_1.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
   - The World Health Organization (WHO) similarly reports only a very slow decline (about 0.2% per year) in intimate partner violence globally. ([who.int](https://www.who.int/news/item/19-11-2025-lifetime-toll--840-million-women-faced-partner-or-sexual-violence?utm_source=openai))

2. **Specific national statistic in Kuwait was mis-represented/mis-quoted**  
   - An article in Kuwaiti daily **القبس** (“Al-Qabas”) shares an official statement by Kuwait’s **Minister of Justice, Nasser Al-Sumait**, claiming a **36% decrease** in domestic violence cases in **Kuwait** during the first **six months** after the implementation of a new domestic violence protection law. ([nabdapp.com](https://nabdapp.com/t/178564790-6e4fd9?utm_source=openai))  
   - According to the same source, the number of cases declined from 1,011 during the equivalent six-month period in 2025 to **646 cases** during that period in 2026. That drop is 36%. ([nabdapp.com](https://nabdapp.com/t/178564790-6e4fd9?utm_source=openai))  
   - The law referred to is **Decree-Law No. 11 of 2026** regarding protection from domestic violence, which, among other things, prohibits withdrawal of the complaint, reconciliation, or pardon in certain severe cases. ([nabdapp.com](https://nabdapp.com/t/178564790-6e4fd9?utm_source=openai))

### What is not supported

- There is **no evidence** found that a “46% decrease” (instead of 36%) for “domestic violence cases” has been reported globally.  
- No independent source confirms the 46‐percent figure. The claims found are localized to Kuwait, and the figure there is 36%, not 46%.

---

## Completed/measured outcome vs. plan/announcement

- **Measured outcome in Kuwait**:  
  The 36% drop in domestic violence cases in Kuwait is a **measured outcome**. It refers to specific data: 365 fewer cases (from 1,011 down to 646) in the specific six-month period after law implementation. ([nabdapp.com](https://nabdapp.com/t/178564790-6e4fd9?utm_source=openai))

- **Pushed claims vs. global plan**:  
  The idea of a “46% decrease globally” appears to be **a mis-quote or exaggeration**—no primary or reliable secondary source supports that exact global statistic. What is documented is a modest, slow global decline in prevalence, not a sharp 46% drop in cases.

---

## Conclusion

- The claim “46% decrease in domestic violence cases reported” is **not supported** by credible global data.
- There **is** a verifiable reported decrease of **36%** in domestic violence cases in **Kuwait** over a six-month period following the implementation of a new domestic violence law. ([nabdapp.com](https://nabdapp.com/t/178564790-6e4fd9?utm_source=openai))  
- Unless more reliable sources emerge, the “46%” figure appears to be incorrect or misattributed.

---

If you like, I can track down whether there are any countries reporting ~46% declines, or whether this number might come from a mis-translation or mis-reporting.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a research note with verified outcomes and details from the major news event titled *“A record-breaking drought tested the Western Slope. Cooperation helped water users get through it.”*

---

### What actually happened

#### Severity of the drought (Water Year 2026)

- Colorado’s Western Slope in 2026 experienced unprecedented drought conditions: record-breaking heat, the lowest April 1 snowpack ever recorded, and exceptionally poor runoff. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- Around one-third of stream gauges (59 out of 178) across the Western Slope recorded their *lowest cumulative water flows ever* for Water Year 2026. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- This year had *twice as many days with record-low flows* compared to 2002, which had been a benchmark drought year. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  

#### Cooperative actions taken

- The Colorado River District activated an *emergency substitute water supply plan* to help mitigate the drought’s effects. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- Key water users in Grand Valley voluntarily reduced their irrigation use early in the season (“voluntarily reduced the senior Cameo demand below its full legal limit”) to help upstream water users and to build storage. ([erwsd.org](https://www.erwsd.org/sites/default/files/2026.06.25_UERWA_PublicPacket_0.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- Releases of stored water were made from Wolford Reservoir and Ruedi Reservoir to protect municipal, agricultural, and domestic users. Together, more than 15,000 acre-feet of water was released for this purpose. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/grand-valley-water-users-conservation-efforts-benefiting-upstream-users-during-historic-drought/article_e2ee4cdb-1dad-45b4-b415-9b2bfd6978d0.html?utm_source=openai))  
- These efforts were collaboratively supported by bodies such as the Colorado Water Conservation Board (CWCB), local irrigation districts (like Orchard Mesa, Palisade, Mesa County), and domestic/municipal districts (e.g. Eagle River Water and Sanitation District). ([cpr.org](https://www.cpr.org/2026/05/22/colorado-river-emergency-water-plan-western-slope/?utm_source=openai))  

#### Outcomes (what was achieved)

- The cooperation and coordinated releases helped avoid more severe curtailments of water for upstream towns, municipalities, domestic users, and agricultural producers. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- About **2,400 acre-feet** of the released supply (out of roughly 15,000 acre-feet) was directed toward domestic and municipal uses to prevent water service disruptions. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- The Historic Users Pool (HUP) in Green Mountain Reservoir, which did *not fill* this year due to drought, had its "hole" (i.e. deficit) partially filled (~15,000 acre-feet total release; the HUP hole) to provide protection for downstream users. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Source evaluation & overlap

- The **Aspen Journalism** article *“A record-breaking drought tested the Western Slope. Cooperation helped water users get through it”* provides both original data (e.g. stream gauge measurements, temperature anomalies) and descriptions of how cooperation occurred. It is one of the primary sources. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Multiple other sources** (e.g. Grand Junction Sentinel, CPR News, etc.) repeat many of the same facts, especially regarding reservoir releases, voluntary cutbacks, and cooperation among water users. Evidence suggests they draw heavily from the same official statements and reports, but some add supplemental local detail (e.g. exact timing, water volumes, participating entities). ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/grand-valley-water-users-conservation-efforts-benefiting-upstream-users-during-historic-drought/article_e2ee4cdb-1dad-45b4-b415-9b2bfd6978d0.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Measured outcomes vs. announcements/plans

- **Measured outcomes** achieved include:
  • Record-low streamflows quantified via gauge data (33% of gauges) ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
  • Specific quantities of water released (≈15,000 acre-feet total; 2,400 acre-feet to domestic/municipal uses) ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
  • Voluntary reduction in irrigation by Grand Valley water users, and the avoided curtailment of upstream domestic/agricultural users. ([erwsd.org](https://www.erwsd.org/sites/default/files/2026.06.25_UERWA_PublicPacket_0.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

- **Proposals/plans** mentioned include:
  • The “emergency substitute water supply plan,” which was approved in advance to enable emergency actions. ([cpr.org](https://www.cpr.org/2026/05/22/colorado-river-emergency-water-plan-western-slope/?utm_source=openai))  
  • Conservation measures like requests to limit lawn watering, urging municipalities to reduce outdoor usage. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/grand-valley-water-users-conservation-efforts-benefiting-upstream-users-during-historic-drought/article_e2ee4cdb-1dad-45b4-b415-9b2bfd6978d0.html?utm_source=openai))  

So, many of the plans were implemented and resulted in actual, quantified water releases and reduced shortages.

---

### Key dates and figures

- **Water Year 2026** spans October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026. Data and impacts relate to that period. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- Approximate **15,000 acre-feet** released from Wolford and Ruedi reservoirs to assist hundreds of users; **2,400 acre-feet** of that went toward domestic and municipal uses. ([aspenjournalism.org](https://aspenjournalism.org/a-record-breaking-drought-tested-the-western-slope-cooperation-helped-water-users-get-through-it/?utm_source=openai))  
- Green Mountain Reservoir’s **Historic Users Pool (HUP)** failed to fill in 2026—an unprecedented event. ([cpr.org](https://www.cpr.org/2026/05/22/colorado-river-emergency-water-plan-western-slope/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Summary

In summary, in **Water Year 2026**, the Western Slope of Colorado faced what many consider its worst drought yet in modern records: historic lows in snowpack, extreme heat, and many stream gauges registering record-low cumulative flow. Rather than mostly battling over scarce water, many stakeholders cooperated: Grand Valley irrigators reduced usage, reservoirs were tapped, and stored water was released to avoid more acute shortages (especially for domestic/municipal users). These cooperative measures yielded measurable benefits—avoiding curtailments, protecting communities, and stretching limited water supplies—rather than just being plans or pledges.

If you want, I can also pull up specific local stories of hardship (e.g. farms or towns that were still severely affected), or ensure what downstream environmental impacts remain.

I searched for credible, up-to-date coverage of the news item “Nā Koa Manu Conservation announces 2026 Dr. Fern Duvall II Dedicatory Conservation Scholarship recipient.” I was unable to locate any original source or independent reporting that confirms **who** has received the 2026 scholarship. Below is a research note summarizing what *is* known, and what remains unverified.

---

### What *is* known

- Nā Koa Manu Conservation, Inc. (NKMC) is a Hawaiʻi nonprofit that supports conservation research, habitat restoration, education, and related work in native ecosystems. ([causeiq.com](https://www.causeiq.com/organizations/na-koa-manu-conservation%2C474189809/?utm_source=openai))  
- The organization has a “Dr. Fern Duvall II Dedicatory Conservation Scholarship,” which is awarded to undergraduate or graduate students studying environmental science, biology, conservation or related fields. The one-time amount is $2,000, subject to available funding. Applicants must have minimum GPA (3.0 on 4.0 scale), show commitment to conservation through coursework, research, volunteer service or community initiatives. Preference is given to those from Hawaiʻi or conducting work in Hawaiʻi. ([mauinews.com](https://www.mauinews.com/news/page/17/?id=569938&page=mscontent.saveContentMsg&utm_source=openai))  
- In September 2026, NKMC publicly announced that applications were open for the 2026 scholarship, with a deadline of October 16, 2026. ([mauinews.com](https://www.mauinews.com/news/page/17/?id=569938&page=mscontent.saveContentMsg&utm_source=openai))  

---

### What *is not* confirmed

- I found **no reliable published source** (news article, press release, or website update) confirming the name of the **recipient** of the 2026 Dr. Fern Duvall II Dedicatory Conservation Scholarship. Neither NKMC’s site nor news outlets had identified the awardee as of the latest checked date.  
- The initial candidate statement (“Scholarship announcement supports conservation efforts with measurable outcomes”) is **not supported** by the sources I located; no measurable outcomes or completed outcomes related to the 2026 scholarship (beyond the announcement of the call for applications) were documented.  

---

### Additional relevant information

- NKMC’s financial data (2024) shows **revenues of about $884,207** and expenses of about $446,899. ([causeiq.com](https://www.causeiq.com/organizations/na-koa-manu-conservation%2C474189809/?utm_source=openai))
